mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average, the real interest rate is expected to decline, lowering discount rates and increasing the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05) during the identified low-rate regime.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in labor force participation (UNRATE) signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as investor caution increases.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < previous 12 months AND UNRATE > previous 12 months
failure_condition: Over the 60-day horizon, 20-day forward returns are positive in >70% of similar labor-market weakening episodes (backtest robustness).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer demand indicators (HOUST) coinciding with rising industrial production (INDPRO) suggests a strong economic upturn, which is associated with higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous 4 months AND INDPRO > previous 4 months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite the signal, and both proxies revert to trend within 2 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over three consecutive months indicates supply-side softness, which typically reduces corporate earnings expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during confirmed supply contractions.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in the CPIAUCSL inflation rate above 3% triggers a preemptive rate hike anticipation, which compresses growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive despite the inflation spike, and subsequent FEDFUNDS remain unchanged.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in job openings (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a tight labor market, which usually supports equity valuations and yields positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous 4 months AND UNRATE < previous 4 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat or negative despite sustained labor market tightness (backtested across 10 similar episodes).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS exceeds 5%, it signals aggressive tightening, which typically dampens credit and equity risk premia, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during such regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in consumer confidence proxies (not available in evidence catalog; fallback: use HOUST trend) combined with weak retail sales (not available) would imply demand softness, but since only HOUST is available, a sustained drop in HOUST below trend for 2 months predicts negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
Note: Since only HOUST is available in the evidence catalog, this sketch uses it as a demand proxy for supply-demand interaction. (This is a modeling constraint, not a real proxy.)
regime_hint: Demand weakness detected via consumer activity
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative when HOUST shows recovery within 4 weeks.
